messages.author: 9856907c817cbce8
messages.subject: Fit Before MIRT
parts:
I want to run an MIRT model with a continuous variable (age) predicting response patterns. The code I have is as follows:
covdatS3 <- data.frame(dataPTS3$Age)
mod2.PTS3 <- mixedmirt(data.activePTS3, covdatS3, 1, 
                       itemtype = 'graded', lr.random = ~1|dataPTS3.Age)

The question I have is whether I have to run the graded model as a single IRT mode i.e. [ mod.1PTS3 <- mirt(data.activePTS3, 1, itemtype = 'graded')] and get good fit before I perform the MIRT analyses above. I would think that by definition having another variable such as age will violate local independence. The reason I ask is that the graded model does not fit (according to the C2 fit statistics) because two items are reverse coded (I tested this theory with a bifactor model where there is the latent construct and then two additional factors for positive and negatively worded items). The scale has good fit in CFA and has a good reliability, I think that IRT is just very sensitive to reverse coding. I have tried to search the literature on this but I haven't found anything. Any help would be greatly appreciated.
-Gene

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Fit Before MIRT
parts:
Fitting the unconditional GRM is a good starting point, at the very least to determine if the measurement model itself works well. And it sounds as though the bifactor model is the model of choice, so you probably want to reflect this model structure in mixedmirt() as well by constructing a suitable model syntax definition to reflect this structure. 

Regarding the C2 statistic, it was noted that the CRAN version was slightly off in version 1.29, so the results may not be overly reliable (though the previous results appeared to be more conservative, so a misfitting model is likely the correct decision anyway. But if you feel like checking, feel free to install the Github dev version yourself). The fit from C2 should be nearly identical to the results you get when fitting similar models with SEM via the WLSMV algorithm for ordered categorical items. HTH. 

Phil

messages.author: 58786c912f9ee9c2
messages.subject: Re: Fit Before MIRT
parts:
W.r.t. to Gene's orginal question on reverse coding: As mirt does not restrict the sign of discrimination parameters, the fit does not change by reverse coding in an uncondtional GRM:

data1 <- simdata(rep(1,5), matrix(2:(-2),ncol = 5, nrow = 5, byrow = TRUE), 500, rep('graded',5))
# reverse first item in data set 2
data2 <- data1
data2[,1] <- 6 - data2[,1] # same number of categories as before with reversed order of labels
fit1 <- mirt(data1,1,itemtype = "graded")
fit2 <- mirt(data2,1,itemtype = "graded")
# identical fit in terms of AIC/BIC etc...

The number of iterations might change (starting values maybe biased towards discrimination parameters with identical resp. positive sign), so if discrepancies in fit occur after reverse coding, convergence problems could be a reason.

Also, local independence should not be violated, if person level covariates are used: After all, one conditions on realizations of random effects (=person parameters) anyway when discussing local independence, so I do not see a problem.

Best,
  Philipp

parts:
Phil and Phillip,
First thank you for the quick responses! Second, I have tried a bifactor mixed mirt model however it fails to converge after 100,000 iterations. The model I specify for the bifactor model (without mixed mirt) is as follows:

model3<-'G = 1-8 
        F1=1,2,3,4,5,6 
F2=7,8'
mod.3BF <- mirt(data.activePTS3, model3, method = "MHRM")

This model fits the data well and converges. Next, I tried to model the bifactor with mixed mirt effects (i.e. age predicting the latent factor). The model is as follows:

mod.4PTS3 <- mixedmirt(data.activePTS3, covdatS3, model3, 
                       itemtype = 'graded', lr.random = ~1|dataPTS3.Age, 
                       technical = list(NCYCLES = 100000))

The mixedmirt function will not allow me to change the method (as I had to do for the bifactor model). Additionally, I'm not sure if the code is plotting age as a covariate for all the latent factors (general factor and the positive and negatively worded items factors). There is not theoretical reasons for age to predict the wording of the factors so if it is attempting to do that is there a way to constrain the covariate to 0 on both of the domain specific factors? Any help would be greatly appreciated.
-Gene

On Fri, Oct 12, 2018 at 8:40 AM Gene a <mos...@gmail.com> wrote:
Phil and Phillip,
First thank you for the quick responses! Second, I have tried a bifactor mixed mirt model however it fails to converge after 100,000 iterations. The model I specify for the bifactor model (without mixed mirt) is as follows:

model3<-'G = 1-8 
        F1=1,2,3,4,5,6 
F2=7,8'
mod.3BF <- mirt(data.activePTS3, model3, method = "MHRM")

Assuming this is the structure you supplied to bfactor(), the model does not converge because it is not identified. You need at least three items per factor, otherwise constraints must be applied. E.g., F2's slopes could be constrained to be equal.

This model fits the data well and converges. Next, I tried to model the bifactor with mixed mirt effects (i.e. age predicting the latent factor). The model is as follows:

mod.4PTS3 <- mixedmirt(data.activePTS3, covdatS3, model3, 
                       itemtype = 'graded', lr.random = ~1|dataPTS3.Age, 
                       technical = list(NCYCLES = 100000))

The mixedmirt function will not allow me to change the method (as I had to do for the bifactor model). Additionally, I'm not sure if the code is plotting age as a covariate for all the latent factors (general factor and the positive and negatively worded items factors). There is not theoretical reasons for age to predict the wording of the factors so if it is attempting to do that is there a way to constrain the covariate to 0 on both of the domain specific factors? Any help would be greatly appreciated.

I don't think there is a way to split the lr.random components across specific factors, yet. Perhaps it should be a feature to be added in the future. The lr.fixed components can do this though by specifying named lists, such as list(F1 = ~ dataPTS3.Age), though I'm unsure whether your age variable should be considered an explanatory variable or residual variance predictor.  

Phil

-Gene
